preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain ownership)

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call setMaxWalletAmount() with a very large _maxWalletAmountPct value (e.g., type(uint256).max) that will cause division to result in zero due to integer division. This will set maxWalletAmount to zero, effectively preventing any non-excluded wallet from holding any tokens, which could be used to trap user funds or disrupt normal token transfers.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has an owner-only function setMaxWalletAmount(uint256 _maxWalletAmountPct) that sets maxWalletAmount = _tTotal / _maxWalletAmountPct. Due to integer division, if _maxWalletAmountPct > _tTotal, the result will be zero. The oracle checks that maxWalletAmount == 0, which can be achieved by calling this function with a very large value.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the contract owner and call setMaxWalletAmount() with type(uint256).max to force maxWalletAmount to become 0 through integer division overflow.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get the current owner address from the contract. 2. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the owner. 3. Call setMaxWalletAmount(type(uint256).max). 4. Verify that maxWalletAmount is now 0.
